goal: Read .xlsx/.xlsm sheets with zipfile + xml.etree in app/xlsx.py (one dataset per sheet), standard library only

acceptance_criteria.text: xlsx.py exposes sheet_names(path) and read_sheet(path, sheet) returning (columns, rows) in the same shape as readers.py

Shared strings, inline strings, numbers and booleans (as TRUE/FALSE) are read; numeric cells with date number formats (numFmtId 14-22 or custom d/m/y) become datetime from the 1899-12-30 serial; the first non-empty row is the header
Sheet XML is streamed with iterparse; a corrupt or non-zip file raises ReadError('not a valid xlsx')
Tests in tests/test_xlsx_read.py use the write_xlsx helper from conftest: Revenue sheet dates come back as datetimes, Lookup sheet reads, broken.xlsx raises not a valid xlsx
Moves acceptance items AC-1, AC-12 forward

decisions.what: Integral numeric cells return int, others float; fully empty rows are skipped; rows are padded or cut to header width
decisions.why: Matches readers.py shape and lets 100+i compare as int; csv does the same width rule

decisions.what: Custom date format detection strips quoted literals, escapes and [..] parts, then looks for d, yy or m with y
decisions.why: Avoids treating formats like 0.00"d" as dates while following the architecture rule

decisions.what: Any KeyError, ParseError, BadZipFile, ValueError or IndexError while reading is mapped to ReadError('not a valid xlsx')
decisions.why: Acceptance says a corrupt or non-zip file must give that note, and scan catches only ReadError per file
